statement: Which of the following lists all solutions to the equation $|x - 6| = 2x + 3$?

choices.misconception: I solved both cases, got $-9$ and $1$, and kept both without checking them in the original equation.
I solved only the case $x - 6 = 2x + 3$ and did not check the answer.
I wrote the second case as $-x - 6 = 2x + 3$, putting the minus sign only on $x$, and kept both candidates.

hints: An absolute value equals either the expression inside or its opposite. An absolute value can never be negative.
Solve $x - 6 = 2x + 3$ and $-(x - 6) = 2x + 3$, then check each candidate in the original equation.
The first case gives $x = -9$ and the second gives $x = 1$. At $x = -9$, the right side $2x + 3$ is negative.

solutions.reliable: Case 1: $x - 6 = 2x + 3$ gives $x = -9$. Case 2: $-(x - 6) = 2x + 3$ gives $6 - x = 2x + 3$, so $x = 1$. Check: at $x = -9$, $|{-9} - 6| = 15$ but $2(-9) + 3 = -15$, so $-9$ is not a solution. At $x = 1$, $|1 - 6| = 5$ and $2(1) + 3 = 5$, so $1$ works. The only solution is $1$.
solutions.elegant: Because $|x - 6| \ge 0$, any solution needs $2x + 3 \ge 0$, so $x \ge -1.5$. That rules out $-9$ before any checking, leaving $x = 1$.
